title: Montara Diagnostics — inference path scouting
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Initial discovery call for Montara Diagnostics exploring Redwood for inference. Discussed candidate open models, context window needs (up to 128k for long reports), multilingual considerations (EN/ES/FR, medical terms), tool-calling for appointment scheduling and EHR lookups, and deployment options (hosted for PoC, dedicated for production throughput, private/VPC for PHI). Agreed next steps: send tailored pricing/latency matrix, share security pack + SOC 2/KMS notes, schedule benchmark window and follow-up SE deep dive on 128k context performance.
next_steps: Samira: Send pricing options for hosted/dedicated/private and an estimated TCO model by 2028-03-27
Ethan: Prepare benchmark plan and sample prompt set for 128k context by 2028-03-29
Marco: Share sample data schema and expected QPS for PoC by 2028-03-24
action_items: Samira Patel: Draft commercial options + simple bill of materials (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
Ethan Cross: Run preliminary throughput / latency spreadsheet templates and share baseline assumptions
Marco Sanchez: Provide sanitized sample document (2–3 examples) and access constraints for PII handling
Rajiv Mehta: List compliance requirements and KMS/HS integration points
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Uh, quick intro — I'm Samira, AE at Redwood Inference. With me is Ethan our SE. How are you all?
[00:06] Dr. Leila Riaz: Hi Samira, thanks, yes. Leila here. Excited to talk — we want to replace some brittle scripts with an inference pipeline.
[00:11] Marco Sanchez: Marco here — platform. We own the infra bits.
[00:14] Olivia Chen: Olivia, product. We're looking mainly at summarization and tool calls to our scheduler.
[00:18] Rajiv Mehta: Rajiv on security. I'll be focused on data flow and KMS.
[00:22] Ethan Cross: Great, thanks. Real quick agenda — 1) hear about your use cases and constraints, 2) model and context needs, 3) deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and security, 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Leila: Yep. High level — Montara builds a transcription to summary system for clinical diagnostic interviews. We also do multi-turn summarization and want the model to reference back into the full transcript when producing findings.
[00:42] Olivia: And multilingual — English mainly but Spanish for ~20% of our user base and occasional French. Also, some French medical terms.
[00:50] Samira: Helpful. Do you have the typical transcript lengths and QPS?
[00:55] Marco: Usually 30–90 minutes recordings. After STT we get 10k–30k tokens per session, sometimes 80k when we keep full multi-session context. QPS is low during ingest but we need bursts for batch processing during clinician review — maybe 5–15 concurrent requests at peak for PoC, could be 50–200 at scale.
[01:13] Ethan: Good to know. So context windows up to 80k and potentially 128k in the roadmap?
[01:18] Leila: Yes, 128k would be ideal for cross-session context, we want the model to look across prior visits.
[01:24] Ethan: Ok — that steers us to models and runtime choices. For open models we usually talk about Llama-family derivatives, Mistral, some of the longer context variants like LongLLaMA forks or specialized 128k window models. They differ in tokenization and memory footprint.
[01:37] Olivia: Are those available on Redwood hosted?
[01:40] Samira: We maintain a model catalog — many open weights are available hosted with performance profiles. For longer context you can either pick a native long-context model or enable chunking + streaming + KV cache techniques. Hosted supports both, but there are tradeoffs between latency and cost.
[01:52] Marco: Cost is a major factor. We want something economical but accurate for clinical nuance. How does quantization affect medical hallucination rates?
[02:00] Ethan: Uh, great question. Quantization lowers compute and cost but can sometimes degrade numeric precision and subtle token probabilities; however, with recent 8-bit and mixed quantization profiles Redwood recommends for production, the delta on factuality for high-quality models is small, though you still need evals on your prompts. We also support hybrid flows — run a cheaper quantized model for initial parsing and a higher-precision variant for final generation.
[02:20] Leila: You mentioned tool-calling. We need the model to call a scheduler, query an EHR stub, and run a reranking service. Do you support function-calling?
[02:28] Ethan: Yes — Redwood supports structured tool-calling and function interfaces. You can define safe tool schemas; runtime enforces size limits and we provide a hook for authorization tokens so the call to your scheduler can use short-lived credentials. There are also retries and circuit-breakers in the call path.
[02:42] Rajiv: From security side, if the model calls external services, what about credentials? We can't leak KMS keys.
[02:47] Samira: For hosted, we recommend using per-call ephemeral tokens and Redwood's credential injection mechanism. For Private deployments, customers have full control — your own network egress rules, private service endpoints, KMS in your VPC. We can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSMs via standard connectors.
[03:04] Marco: That sounds promising. If we wanted to start hosted for speed, then move to Dedicated, then to Private — is that path straightforward?
[03:11] Ethan: Yes — that's the canonical path. Hosted is fastest to get started, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable SLOs, private gives full network isolation. The API surface is the same, so you can pin model versions and rollout rules as you migrate. We can also ship migration playbooks.
[03:26] Olivia: For the long context — do you do on-the-fly retrieval-augmented generation with embeddings and an index, or load the whole transcript into the model?
[03:35] Ethan: Both approaches are used. For extremely long histories, we often do a hybrid: an RAG style index for older sessions and the model's native context plus KV cache for the most recent 20–40k tokens. That gives a balance between cost and fidelity. For 128k native models, you can avoid RAG but backend memory and throughput drop.
[03:52] Leila: What about latency? Clinicians want near-interactive responses during review — <2s for short questions, but longer for full report generation is ok, like up to 10–20s.
[04:03] Ethan: Understood. Latency depends on model size, quantization, batching, and whether you need tool calls. For a 13B long-context optimized model, 2–5s for short answers is often achievable on dedicated hardware. For 70B or above or 128k context, expect higher tail latencies except if you reserve capacity. Redwood's Dedicated plans give you predictable tails.
[04:23] Marco: Tail latencies are our fear. We can't have clinicians waiting 2 minutes. Do you do autoscaling?
[04:29] Samira: Yes — autoscaling for hosted and dedicated, configurable policies for burst, and burst capacity credits for dedicated customers. In Private you run your own autoscaler but we provide recommended configs.
[04:40] Rajiv: Compliance — SOC2, audit logs, retention. We handle PHI so we need strong logs and retention controls.
[04:46] Samira: We support SOC 2 Type II, provide audit logs, and have configurable retention windows. For Private deployments you control logs and retention. We can also sign BAAs for qualifying customers.
[04:59] Olivia: Any concerns about multilingual medical vocabulary? For Spanish, a lot of code-switching with English clinical terms.
[05:06] Ethan: That is common. We recommend fine-tuning or at least prompt engineering with domain-specific vocab, plus targeted evals. Some multilingual models are stronger; others need 1–2k-example fine-tunes. Redwood Optimize can run evals and recommend a model + quantization combo based on your sample prompts.
[05:21] Leila: Does Redwood host the evaluation tooling or do we run locally?
[05:25] Samira: We can do both. Hosted evals let you quickly see model regressions and quality MMR, but for PHI-sensitive data we offer a private eval runner in your VPC.
[05:35] Marco: On data residency — we need EU data to stay in EU region. How is region routing handled?
[05:41] Ethan: Smart routing based on policy — you can pin requests to regions, or use our routing policies to prefer EU regions for EU customers. For Private deployments you deploy in-region.
[05:50] Olivia: For the PoC, we're thinking of a small hosted pilot with a quantized long-context model doing summaries and a tool-call to our scheduler. If that goes well, move to dedicated.
[05:59] Samira: That timeline makes sense. What are your decision criteria?
[06:03] Leila: Accuracy on clinical findings, latency targets, cost per report, and security posture. Also, how easy it is to triage hallucinations and roll back models.
[06:13] Ethan: On rollbacks — Redwood supports model pinning and rollout policies with automatic fallback. If a canary fails QA thresholds, we roll back to previous version. We also emit per-response confidence metrics you can surface.
[06:25] Marco: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[06:28] Ethan: Ideally 2–3 sanitized transcripts representing short, average, and long sessions, plus a prompt set for typical questions and an expected gold summary. We'll run them across candidate models and provide latency/cost/quality tradeoff spreadsheets.
[06:40] Marco: We'll sanitize and share by Friday.
[06:43] Samira: Great. We'll also include a comparison of open models and recommended quantization profiles and an initial cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[06:52] Rajiv: A question about tool-calling security again — can you restrict which tools a model can call and log the payloads?
[06:58] Ethan: Yes — we enforce tool allowlists per model and per route, and tool calls are logged. Payloads can be redacted or stored encrypted and controlled via your KMS policies.
[07:10] Leila: Any limitations around EHR connectors? We don't want Redwood to have persistent access to our EHR.
[07:16] Samira: For hosted we use ephemeral proxies and short-lived tokens. For Private you can keep connectors inside your VPC with no egress.
[07:24] Olivia: Will you share an example of a function schema for our scheduler?
[07:28] Ethan: Yes — we'll include a sample JSON schema and an example of a safe call with token exchange.
[07:34] Marco: On the data plane — do you store transcripts?
[07:36] Samira: By default hosted stores data for X days for debugging, but you can disable or shorten retention. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private or dedicated with strict retention settings. We also support encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed keys for some tiers.
[07:50] Leila: Great. What's the expected cost difference between hosted and dedicated for our workload?
[07:54] Samira: We'll model it, but rule-of-thumb: hosted has higher per-token but zero infra ops, dedicated amortizes GPU cost and is cheaper at scale. Private has additional platform fees but reduces egress and meets strict compliance needs. We'll send a TCO sheet with assumptions.
[08:08] Olivia: Anything else we should know about eval regressions?
[08:11] Ethan: We recommend continuous evals — Redwood Optimize can run periodic checks against baselines and trigger alerts if metrics drop. Also store prompt sets as tests in your pipeline.
[08:21] Leila: Ok, let's recap so we have clear next steps.
[08:24] Samira: Recap: 1) Montara to send sanitized transcripts and QPS numbers (Marco), 2) Redwood to send pricing, model comparison, security pack, and example function schema (Samira + Ethan), 3) Redwood SE to prepare benchmark plan for 128k and candidate models (Ethan), 4) schedule SE deep dive / benchmark kickoff next week. Does that match?
[08:46] Marco: Yes. We'll get the docs over by Friday.
[08:50] Rajiv: I'll compile compliance checklist and share.
[08:53] Samira: Perfect — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the shared drive for artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[08:59] Olivia: Thanks.
[09:00] [meeting ends]
notes: Customer is PHI-sensitive and needs EU-region support and BAA potential
Prefers hosted PoC then migrate to dedicated/private if performance and security checks out
128k context is in roadmap — needs benchmarking; consider hybrid RAG + native long-context approach
